questions.question: What does SLA stand for in ServiceNow ITSM?

explanation.correct: SLA stands for Service Level Agreement. It defines the commitment between a service provider and customer regarding service quality, availability, and response times. In ServiceNow ITSM, SLAs are used to track and manage response and resolution timeframes for incidents, requests, and other task records.

wrongAnswers.explanation: SLA stands for Service Level Agreement, not System Level Agreement
SLA is Service Level Agreement, relating to service commitments, not licensing
The correct term is Service Level Agreement, which defines service quality commitments

source.excerpt: The SLA clock for resolution ends only when the state is set to Resolved.

questions.question: What color indicates a breached SLA in the ServiceNow SLA timeline?

explanation.correct: Red indicates a breached SLA in the ServiceNow SLA timeline. The color progression is: Green (< 50% elapsed), Yellow (50-75% elapsed), Orange (75-100% elapsed), Red (breached), and Gray (paused). These visual indicators help agents quickly identify SLA status.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Yellow indicates 50-75% of SLA time has elapsed, not a breach
Orange indicates 75-100% of SLA time has elapsed, meaning breach is imminent but not yet occurred
Gray indicates the SLA is paused, not breached

source.excerpt: Understand SLA vs OLA vs UC, SLA timeline colors (green < 50%, yellow 50-75%, orange 75-100%, red = breached, gray = paused).

questions.question: What is the difference between a Response SLA and a Resolution SLA for incidents?

options.text: Response SLA tracks time to close, Resolution SLA tracks time to assign
Response SLA tracks time to assign, Resolution SLA tracks time to resolve
Response SLA only applies to P1 incidents, Resolution SLA applies to all
Response SLA is for internal teams, Resolution SLA is for customers

explanation.correct: Response SLA tracks the time from incident creation until it is assigned to an individual (when the Assigned To field is populated and state is In Progress). Resolution SLA tracks the time from creation until the incident is resolved. Both SLAs can apply to all priority levels with different time targets.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is backwards. Response tracks assignment time, Resolution tracks resolution time
Both Response and Resolution SLAs can be configured for any priority level, not just P1
Both SLA types are used for all stakeholders. The difference is what action stops the clock

source.excerpt: Priority 1 incidents should be responded to (assigned to an individual) within 20 minutes from the time the incident is created. Priority 1 incident response time should be tracked through a response SLA.

questions.question: What happens to an SLA clock when an incident is placed On Hold?

options.text: The SLA clock continues running normally
The SLA clock resets to zero
The SLA clock pauses and resumes when taken off hold
The SLA is automatically marked as breached

explanation.correct: When an incident is placed On Hold, the SLA clock pauses (indicated by a gray timeline). The pause condition allows time to be excluded when waiting for external factors like customer response or vendor input. When the incident is taken off hold, the SLA clock resumes from where it left off.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The SLA clock pauses when an incident is On Hold. Continuing would unfairly count time when the agent cannot progress
The SLA clock does not reset. It pauses and resumes, maintaining the already-elapsed time
On Hold pauses the SLA, it does not cause a breach. Breach only occurs when total elapsed time exceeds the target

source.excerpt: SLA timeline colors... gray = paused... Know when SLA clocks start, pause, and stop.

questions.question: Which types of agreements can be configured in ServiceNow to track service commitments? (Select two)

explanation.correct: ServiceNow supports three types of service agreements: SLAs (Service Level Agreements) define commitments between the IT organization and customers. OLAs (Operational Level Agreements) define commitments between internal IT teams. UCs (Underpinning Contracts) define commitments with external vendors. MSC and TRD are not agreement types in ServiceNow.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Master Service Contract is not a standard ServiceNow agreement type. The three types are SLA, OLA, and UC
Technical Requirement Document is not a ServiceNow agreement type. Use SLA, OLA, or UC for service commitments

source.excerpt: Understand SLA vs OLA vs UC, SLA timeline indicators, pause conditions, and breach handling.

questions.question: A company requires that Priority 1 incidents be responded to within 20 minutes during business hours only (8AM-5PM weekdays). Which SLA component needs to be configured?

options.text: The SLA workflow to exclude weekends
The SLA schedule to define 8-5 weekdays
The SLA notification to pause on weekends
The SLA condition to filter by time of day

explanation.correct: SLA definitions use schedules to determine when the SLA clock runs. By configuring a schedule of 8-5 weekdays and attaching it to the SLA definition, the SLA clock will only count time during those hours. Time outside the schedule is automatically excluded from the elapsed time calculation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Workflows are for process automation, not for defining when SLA time is counted. Schedules control SLA timing
Notifications alert users about SLA status but don't control when the clock runs. Schedules define operational hours
Conditions determine when an SLA applies to a record, but schedules determine when time is counted

source.excerpt: Update the existing Priority 1 Response SLA for incidents so that it only runs during the schedule of 8-5 weekdays and the duration is set to 20 minutes.

questions.question: What color does the SLA Timeline display when a task SLA is paused?

explanation.correct: A paused task SLA stage is displayed in gray on the SLA Timeline. Green is <50%, yellow is 50-75%, orange is 75-100%, and red indicates a breach (>100%).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Green indicates a task SLA below 50% of the defined duration.
Yellow indicates 50-75% of the SLA duration has elapsed.
Red indicates the task has exceeded (breached) the defined SLA duration.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: The stage will be displayed in gray if the task is paused.

questions.question: Which two types of service agreements exist alongside SLAs in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: ServiceNow supports three types of service agreements: SLAs (between service provider and users), OLAs (internal agreements to meet SLAs), and UCs (agreements between service provider and external vendors). OLAs track internal service commitments; UCs track external vendor performance.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Configuration Level Agreement is not a valid agreement type in ServiceNow.
Business Process Agreement is not a valid agreement type in ServiceNow.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: Operational-level agreements are internal agreements... Underpinning contracts are agreements that are used to track performance between an external service provider and a vendor.

questions.question: An incident's assignment group is changed during investigation. What happens to the SLA?

options.text: The initial SLA is closed and a new SLA begins with a retroactive start
The SLA is paused until the new group accepts the assignment
The SLA is canceled and no new SLA is created

explanation.correct: When the assignment group is changed, a condition can be set to close the initial SLA triggered and start a new SLA with a retroactive start. Internal SLAs (indicated as OLA in the Type column) may be activated when an incident escalates to a different group.

wrongAnswers.explanation: When assignment group changes, the SLA can be recalculated based on the new group's service commitments.
SLAs are not paused on reassignment — they are closed and new ones begin retroactively.
The SLA is not simply canceled — a new one begins with a retroactive start date.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: A condition can be established to identify when the assignment group is changed. In such cases, the initial SLA triggered will be closed. And a new SLA will begin with a retroactive start.

questions.question: When does the Response SLA end for an incident?

options.text: When the incident state is set to Resolved
When the Assigned To field is completed and state is set to In Progress

explanation.correct: The Response SLA ends when the Assigned To field is completed and the state is set to In Progress. At this point, the Resolution SLA continues to run until the incident is resolved.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Setting the state to Resolved ends the Resolution SLA, not the Response SLA.
The Response SLA ends much earlier than closure — it ends when the incident is acknowledged and assigned.
Caller confirmation may trigger closure but has no bearing on the Response SLA.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: Once the Assigned To field is completed and the state is set to In Progress, the response SLA ends while the resolve SLA continues to run.

questions.question: When does the SLA clock begin counting down for an incident?
options: Once the incident record is saved
When the incident is assigned to an agent
When the incident state is set to In Progress
After the incident priority is determined
questions.correctAnswer: Once the incident record is saved
questions.explanation: Once an incident record is saved, the SLA clock begins counting down. This happens regardless of assignment or state changes. The clock continues until specific conditions are met, such as On Hold (pause) or Resolved (resolution SLA end).

wrongAnswers.When the incident is assigned to an agen: The SLA clock starts when the record is saved, not when assigned. Assignment completion (Assigned To field populated + In Progress state) ends the response SLA, but doesn't start the overall clock.
wrongAnswers.When the incident state is set to In Pro: The In Progress state, combined with the Assigned To field being completed, ends the response SLA. The SLA clock starts earlier, when the record is saved.
wrongAnswers.After the incident priority is determine: Priority affects which SLA definition applies, but the clock starts as soon as the incident record is saved.

questions.question: What happens to the SLA when an incident's priority changes?
options: The previous SLA is canceled and a new one begins, but the SLA clock does not reset
The previous SLA is paused and resumes if priority reverts back
The SLA clock resets to zero with the new priority
The original SLA continues unchanged regardless of priority
questions.correctAnswer: The previous SLA is canceled and a new one begins, but the SLA clock does not reset
questions.explanation: If the priority of an incident changes, the previous SLA is canceled and a new one begins. However, the SLA clock does not reset in this scenario — the elapsed time carries over, meaning the new SLA accounts for time already spent.

wrongAnswers.The previous SLA is paused and resumes i: The previous SLA is canceled, not paused. It does not resume if the priority changes back; a new SLA would be created instead.
wrongAnswers.The SLA clock resets to zero with the ne: The SLA clock explicitly does not reset when priority changes. The elapsed time is maintained.
wrongAnswers.The original SLA continues unchanged reg: The original SLA is canceled when priority changes. A new SLA is created based on the new priority level.

questions.question: What color indicator represents a task SLA stage between 75% and 100% of the defined SLA duration on the SLA Timeline?
options: Orange
Yellow
Red
Green
questions.explanation: On the SLA Timeline, colored indicators show progress: Green = below 50%, Yellow = 50%-75%, Orange = 75%-100%, and Red = exceeds 100% (breached). Gray indicates the task is paused.

wrongAnswers.Yellow: Yellow represents a task SLA stage between 50% and 75% of the defined SLA duration, not 75%-100%.
wrongAnswers.Red: Red indicates that the task has exceeded (breached) the defined SLA duration — over 100%.
wrongAnswers.Green: Green indicates a task SLA stage below 50% of the defined SLA duration.

questions.question: An agent receives a Priority 5 incident. After investigation, the urgency is increased, changing the priority to Priority 4. What happens to the task SLAs?
options: The Priority 5 SLA is closed and a new Priority 4 SLA begins with the elapsed time carried forward
Both the Priority 5 and Priority 4 SLAs run simultaneously
The Priority 5 SLA continues with adjusted targets for Priority 4
The Priority 5 SLA is deleted and a new Priority 4 SLA starts from zero
questions.correctAnswer: The Priority 5 SLA is closed and a new Priority 4 SLA begins with the elapsed time carried forward
questions.explanation: When priority changes, the existing SLA (Priority 5) is closed/canceled and a new SLA (Priority 4) begins. The SLA clock does not reset — elapsed time carries forward. This is demonstrated in the course lab where a P5 incident changes to P4, showing the completed P5 SLA and new running P4 SLA.

wrongAnswers.Both the Priority 5 and Priority 4 SLAs: Only one SLA per type runs at a time. The old SLA is closed when a new one begins due to priority change.
wrongAnswers.The Priority 5 SLA continues with adjust: The SLA is not adjusted — it is closed entirely and replaced with a new SLA definition matching the new priority.
wrongAnswers.The Priority 5 SLA is deleted and a new: While the old SLA is closed, the clock does not reset to zero. Elapsed time is carried forward to the new SLA.

questions.question: What is a retroactive SLA in ServiceNow?
options: An SLA that begins with a start time based on a previous event, such as when an assignment group is changed
An SLA that is applied to incidents after they are resolved
An SLA that recalculates past breaches for reporting purposes
An SLA that applies previous SLA definitions to new incidents
questions.correctAnswer: An SLA that begins with a start time based on a previous event, such as when an assignment group is changed
questions.explanation: A retroactive SLA starts with a retroactive start time. For example, when an assignment group is changed, a condition can close the initial SLA and begin a new SLA with a retroactive start. Organizations should consider whether they wish to implement retroactive SLAs and pause conditions.

wrongAnswers.An SLA that is applied to incidents afte: Retroactive SLAs are not applied post-resolution. They are active SLAs whose start time is set to a previous point in time.
wrongAnswers.An SLA that recalculates past breaches f: Retroactive SLAs don't recalculate past breaches. They establish a new SLA with a start time anchored to a prior event.
wrongAnswers.An SLA that applies previous SLA definit: Retroactive SLAs don't apply old definitions to new incidents. They create new SLAs with backdated start times based on conditions.

questions.question: Which TWO conditions must be met for the Response SLA to end on an incident? (Choose 2)
options: The Assigned To field is completed
The state is set to In Progress
The incident is escalated to Level 2 support
A work note is added to the incident
correctAnswer: The Assigned To field is completed
The state is set to In Progress
questions.explanation: The Response SLA ends when the Assigned To field is completed AND the state is set to In Progress. Both conditions must be met simultaneously. Escalation or adding work notes alone do not end the Response SLA.

wrongAnswers.The incident is escalated to Level 2 sup: Escalation to Level 2 does not directly end the Response SLA. The specific conditions are Assigned To completion and In Progress state.
wrongAnswers.A work note is added to the incident: Adding work notes documents investigation activities but does not end the Response SLA.

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator notices that when incidents are escalated from the Network group to the Server group, internal OLAs are being triggered. Why does this occur?
options: Internal SLAs (OLAs) may be activated when an incident escalates to a different assignment group
OLAs are always triggered whenever any field on the incident is modified
The administrator incorrectly configured the SLA definitions to trigger on all updates
OLAs only trigger when the incident priority changes during escalation
questions.correctAnswer: Internal SLAs (OLAs) may be activated when an incident escalates to a different assignment group
questions.explanation: Internal SLAs, indicated as OLA in the Type column, may be activated when an incident escalates. OLAs are internal agreements that define service targets for internal groups. When an incident moves between assignment groups, new OLAs specific to the receiving group can be triggered to track their internal commitments.

wrongAnswers.OLAs are always triggered whenever any f: OLAs are not triggered by any field modification. They are triggered by specific conditions, such as assignment group changes during escalation.
wrongAnswers.The administrator incorrectly configured: This is the expected behavior, not a misconfiguration. OLAs are designed to activate when incidents escalate to track internal group commitments.
wrongAnswers.OLAs only trigger when the incident prio: OLAs can trigger on assignment group changes during escalation regardless of whether priority changes. Priority changes affect the overall SLA, not specifically OLAs.
